models.author: Amplified Access
models.description:
# Model Summary

Luganda Gemma 1B IT is a fine-tuned version of Google's Gemma 3 1B Instruct model, adapted for English ↔ Luganda translation and Luganda conversational AI. It uses QLoRA (4-bit quantization with LoRA adapters) to add Luganda language capabilities to the base model with only a 52 MB adapter. The model achieves a BLEU score of 13.85 and chrF++ of 46.59 on English→Luganda translation, a significant improvement over the base model's near-zero Luganda capability (BLEU 0.06). It was trained on 94,542 examples derived from the Sunbird SALT parallel corpus covering locally relevant topics such as agriculture, health, and society.

## Usage

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, BitsAndBytesConfig
from peft import PeftModel
import torch

base_model_id = "google/gemma-3-1b-it"
adapter_id = "AmplifiedAccess/Luganda-gemma-1b-it"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(base_model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    base_model_id,
    quantization_config=BitsAndBytesConfig(
        load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
        bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16, bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
    ),
    device_map={"": 0},
)
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, adapter_id)
model.eval()

prompt = "Translate to Luganda:\nThe farmers need better seeds."
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages, return_tensors="pt", return_dict=True, add_generation_prompt=True
).to(model.device)

with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=128, do_sample=False)

prompt_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[1]
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0][prompt_len:], skip_special_tokens=True).strip())
```

Input: English or Luganda text wrapped in a chat-style prompt. Output: translated text in the target language. Important: always load with 4-bit NF4 quantization and use `do_sample=False` for best results. Loading in 8-bit or full precision will produce degraded output since the adapter was trained against 4-bit weights.

## System

This is a standalone adapter model that requires the base model `google/gemma-3-1b-it` to function. The adapter (52 MB) is loaded on top of the base model using the PEFT library. No downstream dependencies beyond standard PyTorch, Transformers, PEFT, and bitsandbytes. The model accepts text input and produces text output only.

## Implementation requirements

Training was performed on a single NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU (15.6 GB VRAM) using Kaggle's free tier. Training time was approximately 8 hours for 5,909 steps (1 epoch). The model uses 4-bit NF4 quantization during both training and inference, requiring approximately 1.6 GB of GPU memory for the base model plus adapters. Inference can run on any GPU with at least 4 GB VRAM. Total compute: approximately 8 GPU-hours on T4.

# Model Characteristics

## Model initialization

Fine-tuned from Google's Gemma 3 1B Instruct (`google/gemma-3-1b-it`) using QLoRA. The base model was quantized to 4-bit NF4 precision, and LoRA adapters (rank 16, alpha 32) were attached to the attention and MLP layers (`q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj`). Only the adapter weights (13.05M parameters, 2.0% of total) were trained; base model weights remained frozen.

## Model stats

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Base model parameters | 651M (4-bit quantized) |
| Adapter parameters | 13.05M trainable (2.0% of total) |
| Adapter file size | 52 MB (safetensors) |
| Tokenizer size | 33.4 MB (shared with base Gemma 3 1B) |
| Max sequence length | 256 tokens |
| Inference latency | ~1-2 seconds per translation on T4 GPU |

## Other details

The base model is quantized to 4-bit using the NF4 (Normal Float 4) scheme with double quantization enabled. The adapter itself is stored in full precision (float16). No pruning, distillation, or differential privacy techniques were applied.

# Data Overview

## Training data

Training data consists of 94,542 instruction-formatted examples derived from approximately 24,000 clean English-Luganda parallel sentence pairs. The primary source is the [Sunbird SALT dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Sunbird/salt), a professionally translated multi-way parallel corpus created in collaboration between Sunbird AI, Makerere University AI Lab, and KenCorpus/Maseno University. Topics include agriculture, health, society, and other locally relevant domains in Uganda.

The data was cleaned by removing duplicates, empty pairs, misaligned sentences (length ratio > 5:1), and very short or very long sentences. Each sentence pair was formatted into three task types using varied prompt templates:

- English → Luganda translation
- Luganda → English translation
- Luganda conversation

## Demographic groups

No explicit demographic attributes are present in the training data. The SALT corpus reflects general Ugandan topics and standard Luganda as spoken in central Uganda. Regional dialects and age-specific language variations are not specifically represented.

## Evaluation data

| Split | Examples | Percentage |
|---|---|---|
| Train | 94,542 | 90% |
| Validation | 5,252 | 5% |
| Test | 5,253 | 5% |

All splits were randomly shuffled from the same cleaned dataset, so there are no notable domain differences between training and test data. Evaluation was performed on a random sample of 100 English→Luganda translation examples from the test set.

# Evaluation Results

## Summary

| Metric | Base Gemma 3 1B (no fine-tuning) | This model |
|---|---|---|
| BLEU | 0.06 | **13.85** |
| chrF++ | 8.84 | **46.59** |

The model shows a 230x improvement in BLEU score over the unfine-tuned base model. Validation loss decreased steadily from 2.01 (step 500) to 1.26 (step 5500), indicating consistent learning without significant overfitting.

### Training loss curve

| Step | Train loss | Validation loss |
|---|---|---|
| 500 | 2.07 | 2.01 |
| 1,000 | 1.74 | 1.73 |
| 2,000 | 1.49 | 1.48 |
| 3,000 | 1.38 | 1.35 |
| 4,000 | 1.29 | 1.28 |
| 5,000 | 1.24 | 1.26 |
| 5,500 | 1.29 | 1.26 |

### Example translations

| English | Model output |
|---|---|
| Five prisoners were released yesterday. | Abasibe bataano baateereddwa ku kkomera jjo. |
| The government take long to pay doctors in public hospitals | Gavumenti etwala obudde bungi okusasula abasawo mu malwaliro ga gavumenti. |
| The professor is the presidential advisor. | Omusomesa ye munnamateeka wa pulezidenti. |
| My father inspired me to become a surgeon. | Taata wange yamukubiriza okufuuka omusawo. |
| How much money did they share amongst themselves? | Baawaddeyo ssente mmeka? |

## Subgroup evaluation results

No formal subgroup analysis was conducted. Informal observation suggests the model performs best on sentences of moderate length (5–30 words) covering everyday and civic topics. Performance may be weaker on very short phrases, highly specialized vocabulary, or topics not represented in the SALT corpus.

## Fairness

No formal fairness evaluation was conducted. The training data covers general topics relevant to Ugandan society and does not target or exclude specific demographic groups. The model translates text as presented and does not make demographic inferences.

## Usage limitations

- Trained primarily on the Sunbird SALT corpus, which covers agriculture, health, and society. Performance may degrade on specialized domains such as legal, medical, or technical text.
- Luganda has regional dialectal variation; this model reflects standard Luganda as represented in the training data.
- The model should not be used as a sole source for high-stakes translations (legal documents, medical instructions) without human review.
- Short inputs under 5 words may produce less reliable translations.

## Ethics

This model was developed to improve access to language technology for Luganda, a low-resource language spoken by over 10 million people in Uganda. Key considerations:

- The training data is openly licensed (CC BY-SA 4.0) and was created by professional translators in collaboration with Ugandan academic institutions.
- The model is released to support research and development in African language NLP.
- Users should be aware that machine translation can introduce errors and should not replace human translation in critical contexts.

# Acknowledgments

- [Sunbird AI](https://sunbird.ai/) for the SALT parallel corpus
- [Google DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/) for the Gemma model family
- [Makerere University AI Lab](https://air.ug/) for contributions to the SALT dataset
- [Crane AI Labs](https://craneailabs.com/) for their pioneering work on Ugandan language models
